cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's Audit Machine test the job schedule of HANGS Construction Services, its work in progress.
Percent complete is cost so far over expected total cost. Every job recomputes.
A change order adds to a contract's price.
One was booked higher than the owner ever signed.
Then it tests each job's cost estimate.
One job's costs jumped about $1.2 million after the year end.
Now it adds up what it found and sets it against materiality.
Then it writes the workpapers and a draft findings memo for the CPA.

All done. Known errors add up to $103,600 of revenue from that change order, under materiality. Bigger judgment calls go to the CPA: the $1.2 million cost jump and about $407,000 of shrinking profit on another job. Eight items stay open. The CPA, a person, concludes and signs. The machine gives no opinion.
